title: Grilled Corn Orzo Salad
subtitle: with charred scallion dressing
menu_blurb: Warm orzo tossed with charred corn, crispy artichokes, edamame and arugula in a smoky grilled scallion and dill dressing.
intro: An incredibly flavorful salad with surprising ingredients that will exceed all expectations. Every time I make it, someone asks for the recipe. My son Max turned me onto this one!
origin: Pasta salad comes from the Mediterranean tradition of serving cold pasta with oil and herbs, like Italian pasta fredda made with fresh vegetables and olive oil. The creamy, mayonnaise-based versions popular today developed largely in the United States during the early to mid 20th century, when convenience foods took off after World War II.

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A griddle, a baking sheet, a pot, and a large serving bowl

steps.title: Cook the orzo
instructions: Cook the orzo in generously salted boiling water until al dente.
Let it cool, but don’t refrigerate it. Orzo is best slightly warm, not hot or cold ☺

steps.title: Pre-cook the vegetables
instructions: Roughly chop the artichokes, spray with a little olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast at 400°F until lightly crispy.
Wrap each ear of corn in a wet paper towel and microwave for 8 minutes. Then char it on a griddle or grill, turning often, and cut the kernels from the cob.
Steam the edamame until al dente, about 3 minutes. Taste and add more time if needed.

steps.title: Char the scallions and garlic
instructions: Trim the scallion roots and separate the white and dark green parts. Set the greens aside.
Sear the white parts in a hot grill pan for 1 to 2 minutes per side, pressing down gently with a spatula. The goal is char!
At the same time, sauté the garlic cloves in the avocado oil on the other side of the pan for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Make the dressing
instructions: In a blender, combine the sautéed garlic, 4 of the seared scallions, the lemon zest and juice, vinegar, olive oil, miso, and ½ tsp salt. Blend until smooth.
Add the dill and blend again until fully incorporated.
Taste and adjust the salt or acidity.

steps.title: Bring it together
instructions: Thinly slice the remaining cooked scallions and the raw scallion greens.
Add the corn, scallions, artichokes, edamame, oregano, arugula, and red pepper flakes to the orzo.
When ready to serve, pour about half the dressing over the top, adding more only if needed. Extra dressing makes a great dip or dressing for another salad.
Taste and adjust with more salt or lemon juice.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more edamame or orzo for a less leafy salad.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Add avocado, charred asparagus, or cherry tomatoes.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: If you won’t serve it all at once, dress only what you are serving and keep the rest separate until you need it.

notebook.question: Is edamame good for you?
answer: Yes! These young soybeans are a complete, plant-based protein packed with fiber, iron, and nutrients like vitamin K and folate. They support heart health, help regulate blood sugar, and may help with weight management.

notebook.question: Are soy products good for you?
answer: Generally, yes. Soy is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein that can lower cholesterol and reduce heart disease risk. Whole soy foods like tofu, edamame, and tempeh are packed with isoflavones and fiber, making them a healthy alternative to red meat.
